name: Mallow Pink
lede: Mallow Pink is a soft purplish pink named for the mallow flower, recorded by the Maerz and Paul dictionary in 1930 with a first use in 1912.

sections.title: A flower pink
sections.body:
Our data traces the name to mallow, the flowering plant, rather than a pigment or a place [1]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 plots it on plate 49 A7 and gives it a first recorded use of 1912, and the ISCC-NBS system files the same area as "moderate purplish pink" [1]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 70, chroma 34, hue 350 degrees: a soft, moderately saturated pink leaning purple [1].

Its nearest computed neighbors are [[kobi|Kobi]] and [[amaranth-pink|Amaranth Pink]], both close by distance, and [[pink|Pink]] itself, 4.0 units off and more vivid [2]. Its sibling in our nature-tier set, [[light-mallow-purple|Light Mallow Purple]], shares the same plant root but reads as a brighter, more purple hue [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in only 3, as photographed (1 by the stricter within-painting measure), which makes it rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track; this is one of the least-represented colors in our data [4].
